risks: The preserved defect_patch_text cannot be applied faithfully as a complete fix: it owns only observed attempts, deletes fulfilled entries before establishing producer quiescence, treats callback result=false as fulfilled work, does not reconcile ambiguous acknowledgements, and swallows the drain error. The additions above intentionally repair those gaps rather than claiming the preserved text already satisfies the gates.

Current drop trace: adapter index.ts discards Promise.resolve(observe(observation)); observe returns admission.callbackChain, whose .then calls async observeWorkerAttempt, which awaits workerLifecycleRunner and subsequent completion work; AgentSession currently forwards the callback directly; AttemptSettlementRegistry Subscriber is void and #notify invokes it without owning its return. The registry remains unchanged because the new synchronous session wrapper captures/owns the return before returning void to #notify; #publish/#deliver remain synchronous.

The producer-fence addition touches src/async/job-manager.ts, which was not named among the originally preserved edits. Omitting it breaks this candidate: AgentSession calls its explicitly defined waitForProducers method. It is needed because dispose() clears #jobs even when jobsSettled=false, and post-clear waitForAll/waitForOwnerJobs cannot establish quiescence.

The producer fence is source-derived, not runtime-proven. Its scope relies on beginDispose blocking new session work, agent.waitForIdle/in-flight-handler drain closing the session's dispatching path, root manager.dispose closing global registration, and the retained job promises covering native job bodies. It does not assert that arbitrary external code cannot later register work through an unrelated session; test root, child, and nested dispatch paths before promotion.

The session subscription remains owned until the consumer unsubscribes. The current Brain adapter unsubscribes on acknowledged completion or its preserved 30-second expiry. A different observer that never unsubscribes will now produce an explicit bounded incomplete result; no other production observer consumer was found in the scoped searches, but broad external-extension compatibility is not established.

The adapter lifetime promise is deliberately outside admission.callbackChain and outside native cleanup. Moving its await into observeWorkerAttempt or registering it as cleanup would create the self-prerequisite cycle prohibited by the task.

The expiry budget still starts during session_shutdown, before native disposal; the host drain's 30-second budget starts later. A very slow native cleanup may therefore outlive subscription expiry. That case is intentionally incomplete and nonzero, not silently successful; this candidate does not extend the existing expiry policy.

The callback-result interface does not expose the durable receipt SHA. This candidate does not invent a client-side SHA or claim an unobserved digest. Reconciliation resends the exact same options/payload and sequence; worker_protocol.ingest_worker_lifecycle already authenticates the attempt/native binding, recomputes canonical receipt_sha256, and compares it with the existing (attempt_id, sequence) row before acknowledging a duplicate. Capture the actual database receipt SHA in the verification evidence. If a client-visible SHA is a hard interface requirement, a separate exact response-field change is required; it is not present in the preserved patch.

Python currently omits identity on rejected callbacks. The bridge change labels the original request identity as rejectedRequest, rather than pretending Python echoed it. Accepted-response identity guards are unchanged. A malformed/mismatched accepted response remains unknown and may get one identical-payload reconciliation resend.

Unknown acknowledgement followed by another unavailable/refused reconciliation is incomplete; neither accepted nor not-committed is inferred. An actual earlier commit may already have released ownership. The patch does not attempt to reverse it or claim the durable row remained held; only a same-receipt acknowledgement or direct durable evidence establishes what happened.

An intermediate explicit callback refusal remains an observer failure even if a later independent revision succeeds. This is intentionally conservative and preserves evidence; the identical-payload unknown-then-reconciled path succeeds without first reporting a failed receipt.

The returned observer promise also waits for the whole prepared mutating batch's subscription outcome. This closes the mixed-batch never-observed gap, but adds one promise and retained admission references per active subscription; successful completion or expiry releases the subscription, and terminal disposal bounds the wait.

Required live dependencies were traced for the current Brain path: the adapter is in-process, the lifecycle bridge uses execFile with its own Python subprocess rather than MCP/eval transport, and the session writer is closed after the proposed drain. Thus no reorder of the existing parallel MCP/eval/title shutdown was included. This is not a general promise that every third-party observer's dependencies survive that block.

print-mode.ts needs no edit for this candidate: its existing dispose catch rethrows non-persistence errors, so the final observer-drain error cannot become normal success there. main.ts's normal postmortem.quit follows awaited disposal. Other exit paths, including AgentSession's extension shutdown callback using dispose().finally(() => process.exit(0)), were observed and are not repaired here; that callback can still exit zero after an incomplete disposal, although the incomplete diagnostic is emitted first. Qualify the actual canary exit path rather than claiming universal exit-code coverage.

Live isolation-runner.ts still contained a second settlement.trackCleanups registration inside deferredCleanup at the time of this read, despite the shared context saying it was removed. It also used agent-label/generation-0 barrier identity. These are source-state qualifications, not included edits; do not silently reapply or expand the cleanup patch from this result.

The full candidate must still be applied with one-match checks, type-checked, and behaviorally qualified by the driver.
verification_steps: Before applying, hash the actual host package and loaded adapter files, record canary version/module-load paths, and require one exact CRLF anchor match per edit. Include agent-session.ts, async/job-manager.ts, attempt-settlement.ts, runner.ts, types.ts, index.ts, prime.d.ts, worker-lifecycle-bridge.ts, worker_protocol.py, cleanup-barrier.ts, isolation-runner.ts, and the actual Brain database/home identity in the manifest.

Run the adapter's existing scoped test entry with its real toolchain: from brainstem/prime-extension, npm test -- tests/worker-context.test.ts. Run npm run typecheck after all driver edits land. The adapter targets ES2022; the candidate deliberately uses new Promise for its lifetime rather than Promise.withResolvers. Host type checking/build validation remains the driver's integrated gate.

Producer-fence scenario: retain a real AsyncJobManager run promise behind a controllable deferred, call manager.dispose({timeoutMs:0}), observe its ordinary job list being cleared, and verify waitForProducers still remains pending until the original deferred completes. Register a replacement under the same job id and verify completion of the older promise does not remove the replacement producer. Repeat with owner filtering and a child session.

Ownership scenario: use the actual registry/session observer path, publish a snapshot synchronously, and have the callback return a delayed lifecycle runner promise. Assert publication returns before RPC completion, but session.dispose does not finish and pre-quit does not occur until that exact returned promise and subscription lifetime finish. Include asynchronous work appended by observeWorkerAttempt after the RPC return; resolving only the scheduling promise must not satisfy the check.

Late-revision scenario: begin disposal while a real registered cleanup promise is pending; let the native manager hit its short dispose timeout; then settle native cleanup and publish a newer terminal revision during the final observer drain. Verify that revision enters the chain, receives its real callback result, and is included before drain completion. Assert an initially empty observer-work collection is not used to bypass the retained producer fence.

Registration/no-observation scenario: register an observer before native begin and never publish a snapshot; expire/unsubscribe it. Expect worker-observer-incomplete plus host drain-incomplete, not successful completion. Also test a mixed batch with one accepted writer, one never-observed writer, and a read-only member: the batch lifetime must reject, and the read-only member must not be submitted as a writer receipt.

Refusal scenario: return real Python-style {status:'rejected', failure_code:'BINDING_MISMATCH'} without identity. Verify bridge output remains ok:false/status:rejected, includes rejectedRequest with the original attempt and sequence, preserves the refusal code, does not call it RECEIPT_MISMATCH, does not retry that explicit refusal, and causes an explicit incomplete observer outcome. Confirm mismatched accepted responses still fail the original acceptance guards.

Lost-ack scenario: use the real Brain callback against a disposable database, commit one receipt, then lose its transport response. The sole reconciliation request must be byte-equivalent in the canonical receipt fields, with unchanged attempt, native identity, sequence, outcome, executorSettled, and cleanupComplete. Query worker_lifecycle_receipts to prove a single (attempt_id, sequence, receipt_sha256) identity and no duplicate transition; require ack-unknown followed by unknown-then-reconciled only after a genuine accepted response.

Unknown-after-resend scenario: lose both acknowledgements or make the reconciliation response unavailable. Expect explicit incomplete/unknown evidence and no local lifecycleRevision or cleanupAccepted advancement based on the missing response. Read the durable receipt row separately; do not assert held/quarantined or released merely from the timeout. No compensating release is permitted.

Real cleanup-failure scenario: inject native isolation cleanup rejection or retained workspace through the existing canary fixture. Verify a failed native cleanup snapshot never becomes releasePermitted, the adapter never sends a synthetic true/true receipt, the lifetime expires/rejects explicitly, and the observer drain does not translate allSettled fulfillment into acceptance.

Evidence chronology must include synchronous full worker-settlement-observed; admission/drop reason with incoming and bound identities; worker-lifecycle-chain-started immediately inside callbackChain.then; rpc-started; rpc-returned or rpc-threw with elapsed time and parsed result; ack-unknown/reconciliation when applicable; accepted/rejected; RPC chain-finished; observer-complete/incomplete/expired; host producer/drain start, completion or incomplete; and pre-quit/actual exit timestamps. Never log callback tokens.

Interpret the logs distinctly: observed without chain-started means work never entered the RPC chain; chain-started plus dropped/refusal identifies admission or protocol refusal; rpc-started without returned/threw before abandonment is in-flight unknown work; rpc-returned ok:false/status:rejected is an actual refusal; rpc-returned ok:true plus durable matching receipt is acceptance. Host drain-completed alone is never a receipt.

Run one bounded real print-mode canary through the loaded host and adapter, not just mock forwarding tests. Observe the actual Python subprocess surviving until its callback returns, session writer remaining open for the terminal records, and postmortem.quit occurring after the final drain. Record a normal accepted run, a refused run, and a bounded timeout run; validate the returned/actual exit status on that real path.

Before promotion, inspect the same database's ordered worker_lifecycle_receipts payloads/hashes and worker_tasks state before dispatch, after the initial receipt, after the terminal callback, and after exit. Keep writer-ownership release, logical task outcome, and observation-drain completion as separate facts. Successor write admission must remain blocked before accepted cleanup evidence and become eligible only after the genuine accepted true/true receipt.
